prompt_final:
The brief injected into every generated image and diagram
(`scripts/generate_image.py` reads this section by name). It exists so
generated artwork reads as a sibling of the product surfaces rather than as
stock illustration.

Palette, taken from `khaotik-ui/tokens/tokens.css` — these are the shipped
values, not approximations:

| Role | Token | Hex |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Deep ground | `warm-950` | `#171615` |
| Ground | `warm-900` | `#1c1b1a` |
| Raised surface | `warm-800` | `#201f1e` |
| Light surface | `warm-100` | `#e9e8e6` |
| Light ground / light text | `warm-50` | `#f5f4f2` |
| Brand accent | `brand-yellow` | `#FFCC00` |

**The brief:**

Dark, high-contrast, warm-neutral. Ground the composition in `#171615` with
raised elements in `#201f1e` and text in `#f5f4f2`. Flat surfaces, no
gradients, no glow, no drop shadows, no 3D or isometric treatment. Geometry
is rectilinear with generous negative space. Lines are thin and confident.

`#FFCC00` is the accent and obeys the same rule it obeys in the product: **at
most one instance per image**, marking the single most important element.
Never as a fill for repeated elements, never as a background, never muted or
darkened — it appears at full value or it does not appear.

No stock-illustration idioms: no rounded cartoon characters, no floating
gradient orbs, no glassmorphism, no neon, no purple-on-white SaaS palette.
Nothing that reads as templated. The register is a maker's logbook, not a
marketing page — confident, plain, and made by people who ship.

**For diagrams specifically:** structural accuracy outranks polish. Preserve
every node, every edge, every edge label, and the direction of every arrow
exactly as given. A diagram that looks better and says something different is
a defect, not an improvement.
